briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Weed Finds Its Footing While D.C. Locks In a Medical Win
briefs.top: Michigan operators are finding room to grow — from JARS' Arizona buyout to a fresh push for more Menominee licenses — even as the 24% wholesale tax keeps fueling lawsuits and a gubernatorial fight. Nationally, a federal appeals court just cemented marijuana's Schedule III status and Compass Pathways' psilocybin data keeps clearing hurdles, giving operators real reasons to plan for growth into 2027.

local.text: JARS Cannabis becomes Arizona's biggest chain — the Michigan-based retailer is acquiring Sonoran Roots and its eight Ponderosa dispensaries, expanding well beyond its home turf.
Muskegon hospitality bet keeps moving forward — Fields Cannary's dispensary-restaurant buildout shows ambitious cannabis retail still has runway in Michigan despite the tax squeeze.
Menominee could add four more dispensaries — a petition drive gathered enough signatures to put a cap increase from nine to 13 stores on the November ballot.

Cannabis industry rallies behind tax-cut candidate — MiCIA formally endorsed GOP nominee John James after he pledged to repeal the 24% wholesale tax, giving operators a clear path to relief on the ballot.

License shakeout thins the herd, but survivors adapt — Michigan's active cannabis licenses fell for the first time since 2019, with roughly 940 licenses now inactive as weaker operators exit and stronger ones consolidate market share.

national.text: Federal court locks in medical cannabis win — the D.C. Circuit rejected a challenge to marijuana's Schedule III reclassification, leaving the rescheduling order in effect and clearing a legal cloud over 280E tax relief.

FDA builds the runway for psychedelic approvals — a new September framework for trial design and REMS requirements signals the agency is preparing a live approval docket for psilocybin and MDMA therapies.

Compass Pathways' psilocybin clears its second Phase 3 hurdle — 39% of treatment-resistant depression patients responded after two doses, with benefits holding for six months and an NDA submission targeted for Q4.
Curaleaf swings for a European crown — its $4-per-share takeover bid for Aurora Cannabis is reshaping the M&A landscape as consolidation accelerates industry-wide.

Full rescheduling still waits on DEA — months after the administrative hearing wrapped, no final decision has dropped and 280E guidance remains murky, leaving operators banking medical wins while the bigger prize stays pending.
